thread:
sam: Quick heads-up — I spun up the new hummingbird-512 embed on staging (hf://hummingbird/xb-512). Running a quick quality sweep across wiki-qa holdouts and a short-query subset. Posting preliminary numbers and notes.

maya: Nice. Which exact evals did you run?

sam: recall@1/5, centroid cosine drift, embedding-norm distribution, and an idflip stability check. Compared fp16 baseline -> int8 per-channel -> PQ compact. Short summary below. :eyes:

maya: please paste numbers when you have them.

sam: Baseline (fp16): recall@1=0.601, recall@5=0.863.
int8 (per-channel, calibrated): recall@1=0.572, recall@5=0.838.
PQ-compact (32-byte PQ): recall@1=0.588, recall@5=0.852.
Short-query subset (queries <= 6 tokens): fp16 r@1=0.482 -> int8 r@1=0.435 (bigger relative drop).
Centroid cosine shift mean ~= 0.028. Embedding L2 norm mean +2.3% on int8. Throughput: fp16 ~250 qps -> int8 ~540 qps (single-gpu staging).

jamal: Oof short-tail sensitive as usual. Did you try clamping or quantization-aware calibration with short-query holdout?

sam: Yep. Quick experiment: clamp activations to [-6,6] during quantize pass and re-run calibration on the short-query holdout. Results: int8+clamp r@1=0.558 (recovers a lot), r@5=0.845. Still below fp16 but acceptable for some workloads.

maya: Can you drop the eval command you ran so we can reproduce?

sam: Sure — command I used:```bash
python eval_embeddings.py \
  --model hummingbird/xb-512 \
  --quant int8_per_channel \
  --quant-clamp 6 \
  --datasets wiki-qa,short-queries \
  --metrics recall@1,recall@5,cosine_shift,idflip \
  --batch 128 \
  --out results/hb-512-int8-clamp.json
```

ciara-bot: eval completed and artifacts uploaded to GCS: gs://redwood-evals/hummingbird/2299901122/ (umap.png, nearest-neigh-diffs.csv, recall-summary.json) :cloud:

jamal: I'll take a look at the nearest-neigh-diffs.csv for idflip patterns. If idflip concentrates on low-norm embeddings that could indicate calibration mismatch.

maya: Another thought — try hybrid rerank: use int8 embed for indexing + CE cross-encoder for top-50 rerank. That often recovers short-tail r@1 with a small latency hit.

sam: I spun a staging A/B with hybrid rerank (cross-enc ce-small). Initial numbers: short-query r@1 up to 0.49 (vs fp16 0.482), p95 latency +16ms. Tradeoff seems reasonable for product teams that care about short-tail quality.

jamal: Good. For the main onboarding checklist: 1) full holdout sweep across datasets (wiki-qa, ms-marco-mini, short-queries, duplicate-detect), 2) idflip heatmap, 3) UMAP cluster purity, 4) throughput/cost calc, 5) rollout plan w/ canary + fallback.

sam: Agreed. I'll queue the full sweep overnight and add a canary config: deploy int8 to 5% traffic with automatic rollback if recall@1 drops by >2% on instrumented routes.

eval-bot: Full-sweep job submitted: job_id=hb-512-fullsweep-2299901122, ETA ~6h. Artifacts will be in gs://redwood-evals/hummingbird/2299901122/fullsweep/

maya: Nice. Once full sweep finishes, can we run the quantization ablation (per-channel vs symmetric, clamp ranges [4,6,8], and per-tensor small-scale) and produce the small report for product? They want a cost/quality curve for Dedicated pricing.

sam: Yep — adding ablation matrix to the job. I'll post results + a 1-page summary.

ciara-bot: Note: added checklist card to project board -> "hummingbird-512 int8 onboarding" and assigned to @sam.

maya: Thanks. If anything looks bad overnight ping me and jamal. Otherwise we should be OK to surface this to the model catalog as "experimental - int8" with recommended hybrid rerank for short-tail-critical apps. :thumbsup:

sam: Will do. Closing for now, will update when sweep finishes.
